questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience studying in another country and preferrably a country with another climate and something that was affordable.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think that some of the courses worked very well, while others didn't. Especially one course where they didn't give us notice on the exam dates was has influenced the grade.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult. I feel like both studies were good at responding to mails, but it had been way easier to have some better guides, so that I didn't have to write that many mails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Very little - I got the mail of a coordinator and brief intro to course selection from the tutors.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult to find rent for under 6 months or a year, but we found something the day before we went to Spain.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Very good decision living in the city, to fully enjoy the experience.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy to select courses, but i wished that we had selected shown us the timetables from home as the courses I chose overlapped and I therefor had to change in the last minute.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Tutors helped us registrate.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Tutors

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not succesfull. I had to change two courses as they overlapped and all courses were taught in the morning in english, so I had to take the only english course available in the afternoon, so they didn't overlap.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask to see your timetable before going there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was very different, some courses had very little workload while others much more.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different we were smaller teams so their was not difference between lectures and teaching practical sessons

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Economics of development, Creating Business, Market research, Quality and environmental management and Strategic business Management II.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Economics of Development and Market Research I

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Very high electricity bills. Going more to restaurants and bars than usual

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Electricity were expensive. Going out ended up being expensive. Public transport was cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of sports were available at a very low cost.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Padle tennis, swimmingpool, the gym. Clubs, bars restaurants and street cafes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out to clubs. See Valencia, Granada

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was actually not that challenging

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join some of the erasmus events to meet some new people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Be prepared that spanish people are not always on time (very rarely) and that you have to insist to get them to help you.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their outdoor facilities, restaurants, clubs and sports.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1)Check your timetable from home 2)Be very certain about their point systems at the exams as they sometimes dont tell you 3) Get good study groups

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that the people you rent apartemnts from can be out to cheat you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends and good experiences

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from friends at home, but it is a good challenge.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
